nurses are available, coordinate, do what's needed, act attentively, use flexible and non-traditional methods, and stand in demanding situations.
nurses are the link between different levels, between professions and between patient, relatives and other health personnel.
nurses are pivotal in the care of patients with life threatening illness, and that they have a role that is comprehensive, complex and demanding.

nurses' role in palliative and end-of-life care.
the role of nurses in palliative care across healthcare systems.
the nurse's role and its importance in palliative care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nurse's role is to provide holistic palliative care to the patient and the family.
nurses need to know and to have access to all the knowledge and skills that are required for palliative care.
nurses need knowledge of palliative care, and knowledge of palliative nursing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nurses' role in palliative work is characterised by the nurse being available and coordinating care.
nurses are available and dedicated to the patients and their relatives.
nurses are a central part of the palliative team.

nurses' role in palliative nursing is to be a link between different healthcare systems and different levels of health personnel.
the nurse's role as a coordinator of care is a central and important part of palliative care.
the nurse is the key person in palliative care for the patient and family.
